method: A JSON Patch is an ordered JSON array of operations, and the tool applies them in order to a deep copy of the parsed document, so a rejected patch leaves the input untouched and no partial result is shown. Every operation needs a string op and a string path; add, replace and test also need a value member, and move and copy need from. Unknown ops, non-string fields and non-object entries are refused before any value changes. A path or from is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer: the empty string addresses the whole document, otherwise it must start with / and each reference token is the text between slashes with ~1 decoded to / and ~0 decoded to ~, in that order; other tildes are left literal. Objects are addressed by own property names only, so inherited names never resolve. Arrays are addressed by a base-10 index without a leading zero, and an index must be below the current length for resolution, removal, replacement and test; add also accepts the length itself to insert at the end, and the token - to append. A - token anywhere except the last token of an add path is refused. add sets an object member whether or not it exists, inserts into an array, or replaces the document when the path is empty; remove deletes an existing member or element and refuses an empty path because the result would be no document; replace rewrites an existing value or the document itself; copy deep-copies the value at from and adds it at path; move reads from, removes it, then adds it at path, refuses a from that is a proper prefix of path, and treats identical pointers as a no-op. test resolves the value at path and compares it with value: numbers compare by numeric value, arrays element by element, objects by identical own key sets with equal values, and any mismatch reports the found and expected JSON. Operation log notes are added, inserted, appended, replaced, removed, copied, moved, unchanged, passed or document replaced. The first failure stops the run and names the 1-based operation index, the operation and the pointer; the original values and all earlier steps are discarded. Limits: 200,000 characters per input and 200 operations. Pure local JSON processing; no storage, uploads or network use.
